title: Two-page technical sprint summary for platform sellers (draft)
content:
Slide 1 — title / one-sentence goal:
Two-page sprint summary for platform sellers: a compact, tech-forward deck to convert platform and infra stakeholders during discovery calls. Goal: enable seller to close a technical qualification and get a canary commit within one meeting.

Slide 2 — context (why this exists):
- Sellers keep asking for a super short, deployable checklist they can use during discovery and internal handoffs.
- Longer battlecards exist but too heavy for a single-call motion; need a 2-pager + speaker notes.
- Audience: Platform engineers, infra leads, SRE/ML infra managers evaluating inference runtime.

Slide 3 — meeting flow (30–40m):
- 0–5m: quick intros + confirm constraints (data residency, throughput, latency SLOs).
- 5–12m: pain & metrics (we ask: qps, p95, token budgets, burst patterns).
- 12–20m: proposed routing + fallback architecture (high level).
- 20–30m: demo / sample latency profile + cost estimate.
- 30–40m: next steps: canary plan and support commitment.

Slide 4 — buyer persona cheat sheet (short):
- Platform Lead (PL): cares about predictability, autoscaling, deterministic latency, security. Use terms: "reserved capacity", "SLA-backed", "VPC control plane".
- ML Infra Engineer (MIE): cares about model variants, quantization, batch sizes, runtime kernels. Use: "quantization profile", "KV cache", "continuous batching".
- SRE: cares about degradation modes, fallback policies, tracing hooks. Use: "canary/A/B rollout", "tracing", "circuit breakers".

Slide 5 — 6 quick technical value statements (one-liners):
- Predictable latency at scale: "reserved pools + smart routing deliver consistent p95s during peak burst".
- Cost controls: "intelligent batching + prefix caching that often cuts per-token cost by 30–60% for chat workloads".
- Simple fallbacks: "policy-based routing to cheaper model variants when capacity constrained".
- Private deployment option: "VPC/on-prem packaging with KMS integration for regulated workloads".
- Observability tie-in: "token-level trace + per-route SLOs for root-cause analysis and cost attribution".
- Developer ergonomics: "same API for hosted, dedicated, and private -> one integration path".

Slide 6 — common technical objections & short scripts (for seller):
- Objection: "We need deterministic p95 for 99% of traffic" → Script: "We recommend Dedicated pools with reserved GPU capacity + per-route SLOs and a circuit-breaker fallback to compatible variants for overload scenarios. Would you like a sample p95 curve from a similar workload?".
- Objection: "Can we run on-prem?" → Script: "Yes — Private deployment + optional air-gapped packaging. We partner on validated HW configs; we can schedule a QuickStart runbook review.".
- Objection: "How do you handle model drift and quality regressions?" → Script: "Built-in evals and prompt-set regression alerts tied to rollouts; we can gate canary percentage on quality metrics.".

Slide 7 — quick demo checklist (what to show in 8 min):
- Show per-route latency dashboard with token-level breakdown (point to cost hotspot).
- Walk a tracing example: request → KV hit vs miss and its impact.
- Toggle routing fallback to show graceful degradation to a lower-cost variant.
- Mock a canary rollout: show metrics changing as percentage scales.

Slide 8 — canary / pilot commitment checklist (operational):
- Scope: target model family + dataset or traffic slice (we need sample traffic).
- Duration: 2 weeks preferred, 1 week minimum for initial throughput validation.
- Success criteria: p95 within X ms, throughput Y qps, no quality regression > Z%.
- Resources: PM + infra contact, sample dataset, slack channel, access plan (VPN / IP allowlist).
- Risk mitigations: fallback policy, reduced traffic weighting, daily monitoring runbook.

Slide 9 — pricing & procurement quick notes (to reference only):
- Quick ballpark: hosted per-token + committed Dedicated pricing for sustained throughput. For pilots we often offer trial credits + discounted initial reserved capacity.
- Procurement hooks: SOC2, contractual SLA addendum, marketplace listing if procurement prefers that route.

Slide 10 — open questions / notes to seller (internal):
- Ask early: what is realistic target p95 and token budget per user?
- Confirm whether customers have strict hardware whitelists for Private deployment.
- Internal follow-up items: add a short sample payload we can run through the demo by next EOD. (Jira: GTMT-212)
- TODO: get a sanitized sample traffic file from SE team (Marco).

Slide 11 — handoff template (email + slack snippets):
- Email subject: "Canary plan + next steps — [Customer] x Redwood"
- Body bullets (short): scope, pilot duration, SLOs, immediate ask (sample traffic + contact for VPN).
- Slack: #cs-handshake draft with ping for infra contact + PM.

Slide 12 — annex / quick references for seller prep:
- Confluence: Seller playbook (confluence:go-to-market/amp-seller-playbook)
- Demo assets: PR 98 in sales-assets repo (link in linked_artifacts).
- Recent benchmark: p95 vs qps chart (internal slide deck: GTMT-Performance-Feb2026).

Notes-to-self (rough):
- Keep the deck intentionally minimal — two pages of slides + one page of speaker notes.
- Need a one-click handoff doc for CS ops to spin up a pilot (that's next sprint).
- Iterate language to avoid "inference jargon" for PL persona; keep kernels/kv cache as second-tier talking points.

Open questions for product:
- Can we publish a short public benchmark comparing Dedicated vs Hosted p95 at 50–500 qps? (ask eng: Marco)
- Is there a one-pager on validated hardware for Private that we can attach for procurement?

End — immediate actions before next sync:
- Aisha: draft the 2-slide deck slides + speaker notes (due in 48h).
- Marco: attach sanitized sample traffic (Jira GTMT-212).
- Sofia: prepare short canary runbook template (Slack DM).
- Jonah: validate demo dashboard queries and share short link.

(Version: draft-iter1 — keep conversational tone; aim to convert technical discovery to a pilot commitment within 2 meetings.)
